architecture.mechanism: Geometric scaling laws for axial flux motors to optimize torque delivery and minimize losses
architecture.intervention: Replace the failing CVT belt-and-pulley system with an in-wheel axial flux motor topology governed by the paper's scaling models to eliminate mechanical slip as the cause of sudden torque loss.
architecture.expected_effect: Direct electromechanical torque delivery to wheels independent of engine status or transmission friction, preventing sudden deceleration events caused by CVT slippage without triggering traditional OBD codes associated with sensor failures.
architecture.falsification_test: Install a prototype in-wheel AFM unit on a test bench mimicking the 2020 CR-V load profile; if sudden torque loss occurs during high-load transients despite the AFM control algorithm adhering to the derived copper loss and thermal scaling limits, the mechanism is falsified.
